## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates production-grade security architecture in distributed Docker environments, focusing on envelope encryption patterns, key lifecycle management, and zero-downtime operations across multi-datacenter deployments.

## Key Concepts

- Envelope encryption with per-tenant Data Encryption Keys (DEKs)
- Vault Key Encryption Key (KEK) and DEK lifecycle management
- 24-hour key rotation with zero-downtime rewrap operations
- Data-plane sidecar decryption at API boundaries
- Edge verifier with SPIFFE SVID validation
- Central SIEM integration through audit sidecar

## Code Example

```yaml
# docker-compose skeleton
version: '3.8'
services:
  api:
    image: myorg/api:latest
    environment:
      - VAULT_ADDR=https://vault.internal:8200
      - SPIFFE_ENDPOINT=socket:///tmp/spire-agent.sock
    volumes:
      - /tmp/spire-agent.sock:/tmp/spire-agent.sock
    depends_on:
      - vault
      - spire-server
  vault:
    image: hashicorp/vault:latest
    cap_add:
      - IPC_LOCK
    command: server -config=/vault/config/vault.hcl
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf
```

## Why This Is Asked
New perspective on observability in docker-dca: centralized, tenant-aware logging across DCs without breaking isolation. Demonstrates practical sidecar patterns and integration with Fluent Bit.

## Key Concepts
- Logging sidecar pattern for per-service observability
- Docker Config for tenant definitions and secure config delivery
- TLS termination at Nginx edge and service-side TLS
- Shared log volume and Fluent Bit for central sink
- End-to-end validation of tenant-scoped logs

## Code Example
```yaml
# docker-compose.yml (skeleton)
version: '3.8'
services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:latest
    ports:
      - "443:443"
  api:
    image: myapi:latest
    environment:
      - TENANT=${TENANT}
    depends_on:
      - logging_sidecar
    networks:
      - appnet
  logging_sidecar:
    image: logging-sidecar:latest
    volumes:
      - logs:/var/log/api
    environment:
      - LOG_DIR=/var/log/api
    depends_on:
      - api
volumes:
  logs:
networks:
  appnet:
    external: true
```

local key = KEYS[1]
local rate = tonumber(ARGV[1])
local burst = tonumber(ARGV[2])
local now = tonumber(ARGV[3])
local tokens = tonumber(redis.call('GET', key) or burst)
if tokens < 1 then
  return -1
end
redis.call('DECR', key)
redis.call('EXPIREAT', key, now + rate)
return tokens - 1

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question tests the ability to design end-to-end observability in a multi-DC, TLS-protected microservice environment. It validates understanding of cross-DC trace propagation, per-tenant context isolation, centralized collection, and sampling strategies.

## Key Concepts

- OpenTelemetry instrumentation (automatic and manual)
- OTLP exporter and collector configuration
- Trace context propagation across proxies (W3C traceparent, X-Tenant)
- Tenant-scoped sampling and data governance
- Multi-DC failover and consistent trace routing
- TLS termination at Traefik edge proxy

## Bootstrap Commands

```bash
# Generate TLS certificates
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \\
  -keyout traefik/tls.key -out traefik/tls.crt \\
  -subj "/CN=api.example.com"

# Start the stack
docker-compose up -d
```

## Minimal docker-compose.yml Skeleton

```yaml
version: '3.8'
services:
  traefik:
    image: traefik:v3.0
    command:
      - --api.insecure=true
      - --providers.docker
      - --entrypoints.web.address=":443"
      - --entrypoints.web.tls
    ports:
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro
      - ./traefik/tls.crt:/tls.crt
      - ./traefik/tls.key:/tls.key
    labels:
      - traefik.tls.creds=true

  otel-collector:
    image: otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib:0.110.0
    command: ["--config=/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml"]
    volumes:
      - ./otel-collector-config.yaml:/etc/otel-collector-config.yaml:ro
    ports:
      - "4317:4317"   # OTLP gRPC
      - "4318:4318"   # OTLP HTTP
      - "16686:16686" # Jaeger UI

  api-service:
    build: ./api
    environment:
      - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
      - OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=api-service
      - OTEL_PROPAGATORS=tracecontext,b3
    labels:
      - traefik.enable=true
      - traefik.http.routers.api.tls=creds
      - traefik.http.routers.api.rule=Host(`api.example.com`)

networks:
  default:
    name: dca-network
```

## OTLP Collector Config (tenant-scoped sampling)

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4317
      http:
        endpoint: 0.0.0.0:4318

processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 10s

  probabilistic:
    sampling_percentage: 10

  filter:
    spans:
      exclude:
        match_type: strict
        attributes:
          - key: tenant.id
            value: "low-priority"

exporters:
  otlp/tempo:
    endpoint: tempo:4317
    tls:
      insecure: false

  jaeger:
    endpoint: jaeger:14250
    tls:
      insecure: false

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      - receivers: [otlp]
      - processors: [batch, probabilistic, filter]
      - exporters: [otlp/tempo, jaeger]
```
